b: Aside from one last Starlink Team Series event, the 2026 Major League Fishing tournament season is over. That means it’s time to start looking ahead to 2027, particularly the biggest event on the MLF calendar – REDCREST.

The final three spots in the REDCREST 2027 field were handed out during the recent Toyota Series Championship on Pickwick Lake, and the 40-angler field is now set to battle for the $300,000 title April 16-18 on Logan Martin Lake.

The top 28 finishers from the Fishing Clash Angler of the Year standings on the Bass Pro Tour all earned invitations to compete in REDCREST, and double-qualifiers (or in the case of Drew Gill and Banks Shaw, triple-qualifiers) pushed that number to the top 33. The champion of each Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit event also earned REDCREST invitations, as did the winners of the Phoenix Bass Fishing League All-American and the Toyota Series Championship. Matthew Knopp will represent the Columbia PFG College Fishing ranks after he won the College Fishing National Championship on Lake Murray and beat out his Lander University teammate, Logan Russell, at the Toyota Series Championship. Finally, Japan’s Yuma Ejiri will round out the field as the highest-finishing angler from the MLF International Division on Pickwick.

In all, the field will include three past REDCREST winners (including three-time champ Dustin Connell, who just so happens to live near the Coosa River) and eight former Bassmaster Classic/Forrest Wood Cup/TITLE winners.
